title: Composition of morphisms of sites (Stacks 03CB)
statement: Let $\mathcal C_1,\mathcal C_2,\mathcal C_3$ be sites, each a site in the sense of Stacks Sites, Definition 00VH: a category whose objects and morphisms form sets, with a set $\operatorname{Cov}$ of families $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ (coverings) such that every isomorphism $\{V\to U\}$ is a covering, if $\{U_i\to U\}_{i}$ and $\{V_{ij}\to U_i\}_{j}$ for every $i$ are coverings then $\{V_{ij}\to U\}_{i,j}$ is a covering, and for a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and a morphism $V\to U$ the fibre products $U_i\times_UV$ exist and $\{U_i\times_UV\to V\}$ is a covering. A sheaf of sets (resp. of abelian groups) on a site is a presheaf $\mathcal F$ of sets (resp. abelian groups) such that for every covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ the diagram $\mathcal F(U)\to\prod_i\mathcal F(U_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\mathcal F(U_i\times_UU_j)$ is an equalizer (Sites, Definitions 00VM and 00VR; [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects]); morphisms are natural transformations. For a continuous functor $w:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between such sites (Sites, Definition 00WV: $w$ carries coverings $\{V_i\to V\}$ to coverings and the canonical maps $w(T\times_VV_i)\to w(T)\times_{w(V)}w(V_i)$ are isomorphisms) write $w^s\mathcal G=\mathcal G\circ w$ for sheaves $\mathcal G$ on $\mathcal D$ (a sheaf on $\mathcal C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf]) and $w_s$ for its left adjoint $\mathcal F\mapsto(w_p\mathcal F)^\#$ of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction], on sheaves of sets and on abelian sheaves. Let $u:\mathcal C_2\to\mathcal C_1$ and $v:\mathcal C_3\to\mathcal C_2$ be continuous functors such that $u_s$ and $v_s$ on sheaves of sets are exact (commute with finite limits and finite colimits, Categories Definition 0034), i.e. $u$ and $v$ define morphisms of sites $f:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_2$, $g:\mathcal C_2\to\mathcal C_3$ (Sites, Definition 00X1). Then: (1) $u\circ v:\mathcal C_3\to\mathcal C_1$ is continuous; (2) $(u\circ v)^s=v^s\circ u^s$ as functors, on sheaves of sets and on abelian sheaves; (3) there is a unique isomorphism of functors $(u\circ v)_s\cong u_s\circ v_s$ (on sheaves of sets, and likewise on abelian sheaves) compatible with the adjunctions, i.e. carrying the unit of $(u\circ v)_s\dashv(u\circ v)^s$ to the unit $v^s\eta_u v_s\circ\eta_v$ of the composite adjunction $u_sv_s\dashv v^su^s$; (4) $(u\circ v)_s$ on sheaves of sets is exact, so $u\circ v$ defines a morphism of sites $g\circ f:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_3$ (Sites, Definition 03CC), with $(g\circ f)_*=g_*\circ f_*$ and $(g\circ f)^{-1}\cong f^{-1}\circ g^{-1}$. (Stacks Sites, Lemma 03CB and the remark after Definition 03CC.)
